summary: verdaccio-okta-oauth preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated opaque payload
details: package.json declares preinstall=node setup.mjs. setup.mjs is identifier-obfuscated (hex-suffixed variable names, string-property indirection) and, at npm install time, either invokes an existing bun binary or downloads Bun v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip into a tempdir, chmods it 0755, and execFileSyncs the sibling math_init.js under that freshly downloaded runtime. math_init.js is a ~720KB Bun-CJS bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, shuffled string-array obfuscation, no readable identifiers) and is not declared in package.json `files` (which lists only bin, dist, src) — it ships at the tarball root outside the published-files manifest. A Verdaccio Okta OAuth auth plugin has no legitimate need to fetch a second JavaScript runtime and execute an opaque bundle under it; this is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern (payload executed by a runtime the Node ecosystem's scanners do not introspect).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
